2026-10-12

Import data

Marine_Data_Set <- read.csv("2023, 2024 and 2026 Portelet transects 2.csv")

Convert species columns to numeric format and transpose data from wide to long format,

keeping the quadrat, transect, site and year information and storing species names and

counts in separate columns.

Pivot_Longer_Data <- Marine_Data_Set %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      -c(Quadrat, Transect, Site, Year),
      ~ as.numeric(as.character(.x)))) %>%
  
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Quadrat, Transect, Site, Year),
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "Count")

print(Pivot_Longer_Data)

Calculating the Mean for individual species between all sites

mean_by_species_and_Sites <- Pivot_Longer_Data %>%
  group_by(Species, Site) %>%
  summarise(Mean_Count = mean(Count, na.rm = TRUE))
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by Species and Site.
## ℹ Output is grouped by Species.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(Species, Site))` for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
mean_by_species_and_Sites

Sub setting the pivoted data set to only 7 species of seaweed / algae

sub_set_species <- subset(
  Pivot_Longer_Data,
  Species == "Ulva.intestinalis" | Species == "Corallina.officinalis" | Species == "Corallina.officinalis" | Species == "Fucus.serratus" | Species == "Lithophyllum.sp." | Species == "Cladophora.sp." | Species == "Fucus.vesiculosus")

Calculating the Mean for the sub set species between all sites

mean_by_Sub_species_and_Sites <- sub_set_species %>%
  group_by(Species, Site) %>%
  summarise(Mean_Count = mean(Count, na.rm = TRUE))
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by Species and Site.
## ℹ Output is grouped by Species.

Plotting histograms for each individual sub set species

Histogram_For_Individual_Sub_Set_Species <- ggplot(sub_set_species, aes(x = Count)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_wrap(~Species)
Histogram_For_Individual_Sub_Set_Species
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

# Plotting normal Q-Q plot for species counts

qqnorm(sub_set_species$Count)
qqline(sub_set_species$Count, col = "red", lwd = 2)

Plotting normal Q-Q plots individually for all six sub set species based on their counts

ggplot(sub_set_species, aes(sample = Count)) +
  stat_qq() + labs(x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles", title = "Normal Q-Q Plot") +
  stat_qq_line(colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~Species, scales = "free")

Performing a glm using Count as the response variable and Species as the predictor

variable

glm1 <- glm(Count ~ Species, family = "poisson", data = sub_set_species)
anova(glm1)
## Analysis of Deviance Table
## 
## Model: poisson, link: log
## 
## Response: Count
## 
## Terms added sequentially (first to last)
## 
## 
##         Df Deviance Resid. Df Resid. Dev  Pr(>Chi)    
## NULL                     1139      13688              
## Species  5   664.69      1134      13023 < 2.2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Plotting diagnostic plots using residuals for glm1

plot(fitted(glm1),resid(glm1))

qqnorm(resid(glm1))
qqline(resid(glm1))

hist(resid(glm1))

acf(resid(glm1))

geom_col is used instead of geom_bar as geom_col uses the existing values in Total_Count

while geom_bar counts the number of observation in each species.

Sub_species_Bar_Beauport <- ggplot(subset(sub_set_species, Site == "Beauport"), mapping = aes(x = Species, y = Count, fill = Species)) + geom_col()
Sub_species_Bar_Beauport

Sub_species_Bar_Ouaisne <- ggplot(subset(sub_set_species, Site == "Ouaisne"), mapping = aes(x = Species, y = Count, fill = Species)) + geom_col()
Sub_species_Bar_Ouaisne

Sub_species_Bar_Portelet <- ggplot(subset(sub_set_species, Site == "Portelet"), mapping = aes(x = Species, y = Count, fill = Species)) + geom_col()
Sub_species_Bar_Portelet

Patchwork package to multi-panel figure

Multi_Panel_Plot <- Sub_species_Bar_Beauport + Sub_species_Bar_Ouaisne +
 Sub_species_Bar_Portelet +  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
Multi_Panel_Plot

Using the plot_layout() to specify two columns rather than 3 (as above)

Multi_Panel_Plot_2_Columns <- Multi_Panel_Plot <- Sub_species_Bar_Beauport + Sub_species_Bar_Ouaisne +
 Sub_species_Bar_Portelet +  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") + plot_layout(ncol = 2)
Multi_Panel_Plot_2_Columns

Facet_Wrapped_Sub_Set_Bar <- ggplot(data = sub_set_species,  mapping = aes(x = Year, y = Count, fill = Species)) +
  geom_col() +  facet_wrap(~Site)

Facet_Wrapped_Sub_Set_Bar

Using the above transposed data, grouping the values by site and species, groups

data into three data points per species (1 per site)

combined_Sub_Set_Data <- sub_set_species %>%
  group_by(Site, Species) %>%
  summarise(Total_Count = sum(Count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

Using the subset() function to now create site specific datasets for Beauport, Quaisne, and Portelet

Beauport <- subset(combined_Sub_Set_Data, Site == "Beauport")

Ouaisne <- subset(combined_Sub_Set_Data, Site == "Ouaisne")

Portelet <- subset(combined_Sub_Set_Data, Site == "Portelet")

Performing a Chi-Squared goodness of fit test to test the Difference in species abundance within site

beauport_Chi_Res <- chisq.test(Beauport$Total_Count)
print(beauport_Chi_Res)
## 
##  Chi-squared test for given probabilities
## 
## data:  Beauport$Total_Count
## X-squared = 245.14, df = 5, p-value < 2.2e-16

Performing a Chi-Squared test of independence to test the Difference in species abundance between sites

# Create a species-by-site contingency table
species_table <- xtabs(Total_Count ~ Species + Site, data = combined_Sub_Set_Data)

# View the table
species_table
##                        Site
## Species                 Beauport Ouaisne Portelet
##   Cladophora.sp.              56       0      119
##   Corallina.officinalis      175      16      320
##   Fucus.serratus             171     415      122
##   Fucus.vesiculosus            1     210       56
##   Lithophyllum.sp.           198     102      275
##   Ulva.intestinalis          145     199      469
# Run the chi-squared test
chi_square_independece <- chisq.test(species_table)
print(chi_square_independece)
## 
##  Pearson's Chi-squared test
## 
## data:  species_table
## X-squared = 966.55, df = 10, p-value < 2.2e-16

Using the subset() function to subset the combined data into site specific

data sets for total species

Beauport_Subset_Total_Species <- subset(combined_Sub_Set_Data, combined_Sub_Set_Data$Site == "Beauport")

Calculating species richness at individual sites using the specnumber() function

Species_Richness_Beauport_Total <- specnumber(Beauport_Subset_Total_Species$Total_Count)
print(Species_Richness_Beauport_Total)
## [1] 6

Performing a Shannon-Wiener index on total species at individual sites

shannon_index_Beauport_Total <- diversity(Beauport_Subset_Total_Species$Total_Count, index = "shannon")
print(shannon_index_Beauport_Total)
## [1] 1.551475

Performing Simpson index on subset species at individual sites

simpson_index_Beauport <- diversity(Beauport$Total_Count, index = "simpson")
print(simpson_index_Beauport)
## [1] 0.7785652

Performing Pilou’s eveness index on subset species at individual sites

evenness_Beauport  <- shannon_index_Beauport_Total / log(length(Beauport_Subset_Total_Species$Total_Count))
print(evenness_Beauport)
## [1] 0.8658947
